definition: Intellectualization is a defense mechanism in which a person responds to something threatening by dealing with it through thinking, analysis, or attempts at mental control. In this approach-oriented style, the threat is engaged rather than pushed out of awareness.

provenance.scope: Source record D012095; pinned source text

reasons: The final clause about the threat being “engaged rather than pushed out of awareness” is not supported by the packet; the source only contrasts intellectualization as an approach/control response with repression as an avoidance response.

The definition states that the person deals with the threat “through thinking, analysis, or attempts at mental control,” but the packet only specifies intellectualization as involving “approaching or controlling the stimulus” and does not mention thinking/analysis as the mechanism.

The definition says the threat is “engaged rather than pushed out of awareness”; the packet contrasts intellectualization with “repression” involving “unconscious denial in avoiding the stimulus,” which does not explicitly support the phrase “pushed out of awareness.”
